steps: Create an API key in the Higgsfield Console; it has a key ID and a secret
You enter both yourself: switchboard connect higgsfield --field key_id=${vault:higgsfield_key_id} --field key_secret=${vault:higgsfield_key_secret}  (store each with switchboard vault set first)
No identity probe is defined, so the account is stored but not verified until a real call succeeds
notes: Observed 2026-10-23 (Higgsfield authentication doc): the credential is Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET against https://api.higgsfield.ai; the older hf-api-key and hf-secret headers still work but new integrations should use Authorization. Invalid credentials return 401 with a detail body.
The doc names no read-only account or balance endpoint (its only example is a request-status lookup that needs an existing request id), so this definition has no identity_probe.

LOCKED DECISION (owner, 2026-09-30, CLAUDE.md HIGGSFIELD-API EXCEPTION): Higgsfield developer API calls go through the local higgsfield-api MCP server, which holds the key in Windows Credential Manager, quotes before it spends and enforces server-side caps. This definition exists for completeness and credential custody only; do not route generation through a Switchboard toolkit.
